data.taskBrief:
TASK BRIEF: Discover OpenRouter video models, submit video jobs, poll their status, and download the generated output (OpenRouter API)

FIT
Fully. The supplied requests cover model discovery, job submission, status polling, and content download, which together satisfy the full workflow and the implementation/limit-checking part of the task.

AUTH
Bearer token authentication.
Header: Authorization: Bearer <bearerToken>

BASE URL
https://openrouter.ai/api/v1

STEPS
1. GET /videos/models
   Params:
     Header Accept: string — application/json
   Returns:
     200 with data[]: each model includes id, name, canonical_slug, created, description, generate_audio, pricing_skus, seed, supported_aspect_ratios, supported_durations, supported_frame_images, supported_resolutions, supported_sizes, allowed_passthrough_parameters, creativity, and optional upscale_factor fields.
     400 with error.code and error.message.
     500 with error.code and error.message.
   Threading:
     None

2. POST /videos
   Params:
     Header Accept: string — application/json
     Header Content-Type: string — application/json
     Body (JSON):
       model: string — example from step 1, such as google/veo-3.1
       prompt: string — user-supplied prompt, e.g. prompt-here
       aspect_ratio: string — e.g. 16:9
       duration: integer/string as provided by the schema example — e.g. 8
       resolution: string — e.g. 720p
       Also accepts: callback_url, creativity, frame_images, generate_audio, input_references, previous_job_id, provider, seed, session_id, size, trace, upscale_factor, user — see the request schema for details.
   Returns:
     202 with id, generation_id, polling_url, status, and optionally expires_at, unsigned_urls[], usage.cost, and usage.is_byok.
     400 with error.code and error.message.
     401 with error.code and error.message.
   Threading:
     Uses model information from step 1 when choosing a supported model; all other required values come from the caller or the task context.

3. GET /videos/{jobId}
   Params:
     Header Accept: string — application/json
     Path jobId: string — the video job ID returned by step 2 (for example, job-abc123)
   Returns:
     200 with id, generation_id, polling_url, status, and when completed unsigned_urls[] plus usage.cost.
     401 with error.code and error.message.
     403 with error.code and error.message.
     404 with error.code and error.message.
     500 with error.code and error.message.
   Threading:
     jobId from step 2

4. GET /videos/{jobId}/content
   Params:
     Header Accept: string — video/mp4
     Path jobId: string — the video job ID returned by step 2 or confirmed in step 3
     Query index: integer — example 0; provided in the request schema and used to select a content item when applicable
   Returns:
     200 streams raw video bytes.
     400 with error.code and error.message.
     401 with error.code and error.message.
     403 with error.code and error.message.
     404 with error.code and error.message.
     409 with error.code and error.message.
     410 with error.code and error.message.
     500 with error.code and error.message.
     502 with error.code and error.message.
   Threading:
     jobId from step 2 or 3

GOTCHAS
- All authenticated calls need the Authorization header; the examples show 401 when it is missing.
- POST /videos is JSON; send Content-Type: application/json.
- Use a model supported by /videos/models; the example model supports only 16:9, 5 or 8 second durations, 720p, and first_frame/last_frame frame images.
- The job ID from POST /videos is required for both polling and content download.
- /videos/{jobId}/content returns raw video bytes, not a JSON document, even though the saved error examples are JSON.
